report.source_text: After consultation with the oncology team, long-acting octreotide 30 mg monthly was suggested. The patient was discharged, but a few days later, he complained from perioral, hand, and feet paresthesia and numbness and developed symptomatic hypocalcemia; his corrected calcium level was 6.5 mg/dl, phosphate level was 2.5 mg/dl, 25 hydroxy vitamin D level was 22.8 ng/ml, and the PTH level was 107 pg/ml. He received intravenous and oral calcium accompanied by 50,000 units of oral ergocalciferol weekly. The symptoms were relieved, and the calcium level was corrected
